subject.title: fix(config): allow Nix-mode doctor --fix for non-config writes

question: Should Nix mode continue refusing doctor repair mode before side effects, or may doctor apply non-config repairs before failing on a later openclaw.json mutation?
rationale: Both behaviors are technically possible, but they define different guarantees for declarative installations and partial repair outcomes; the current shipped policy deliberately chose fail-fast semantics.

options.title: Keep Fail-Fast Policy
options.body: Close this PR and retain the shipped guarantee that Nix-mode doctor repairs make no repair side effects.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped Repairs
options.body: Require a revised implementation that identifies a provably config-free repair plan before applying any state changes.

options.title: Accept Partial Repairs
options.body: Explicitly approve the proposed behavior, document partial completion semantics, and require upgrade proof covering mixed state/config repair runs.

recommendation.title: Keep Fail-Fast Policy
recommendation.body: Close this PR and retain the shipped guarantee that Nix-mode doctor repairs make no repair side effects.

likelyOwner.reason: This changes the repository-wide policy for declarative Nix installations and needs product-level ownership beyond the implementation author.
